Resolved by three commits on `main`:

- `7435c290` — `scripts/okf.kuki` gained a `--refresh` mode (bump `generated.at`/`stale_after` on the given paths, preserving `by` and a blank `verified`; handles both the inline flow-map and block-map `generated:` forms). `scripts/pre-commit` runs it over every staged `.md` **before** the empty-`$DIFF` early exit — skipping files with unstaged edits so it cannot sweep unrelated work — so a doc-only commit is refreshed too. The doc-sync prompt now also instructs the LLM to refresh OKF metadata, and AGENTS.md rule `pre-commit-hook` names the deterministic step.
- `27790ffc` — `make okf-refresh-check`, a red-first pin (proves the fixture is actually stale, runs `--refresh`, then asserts the bump, the preserved `by`/`verified`, and the untouched body), wired into `release-check`.
- `382e3860` — frontmatter-only refresh of the nine pre-existing stale docs (`cmd/SKILL.md`, `kukicha/SKILL.md`, `release/SKILL.md`, `WIRE-CONTRACTS.md`, `SHARP-EDGES.md`, `DIAGNOSTIC-PARITY.md`, `SQLITE-VECTOR-SIMD-PLAN.md`, two tutorials).

Root cause 1 (the agent never refreshed the header) is now deterministic, and root cause 2 (doc-only commits skipped doc-sync entirely) is closed. For root cause 3 (nothing caught it) I deliberately did **not** add a repo-wide "`generated.at` predates the last commit" gate: a tolerance is required because an edit always precedes its commit, and even a 1-hour tolerance flagged docs only minutes-to-hours out — too noisy to gate. The deterministic hook plus `okf-refresh-check` is the enforcement instead; `make okf-lint` remains a shape/expiry lint.

Verified: `bash -n scripts/pre-commit`, `make okf-lint` (40 docs checked, 0 issues), `make okf-refresh-check`, `make check-kuki` (25 targets), `make fmt-check`, and `go test -run TestNoDanglingDocReferences .` — all green. Self-hosting confirmed: committing the hook change ran the new step and bumped AGENTS.md's own `generated.at`.

# semantic: local variant-typed values lose `unknown-method`/`unknown-field` (check-green, `go build`-red)

## Summary
`8724e1fd` made `typeAnnotationToTypeInfo` resolve a local variant annotation to `TypeKindVariant`. `resolveFieldType`/`resolveMethodType` return `(nil, false)` for any kind other than `TypeKindNamed`/`TypeKindStruct`, so a member miss on a locally variant-typed value is no longer diagnosed — `kukicha check` passes and `go build` fails. Introduced by that commit (the parent diagnosed it).

## Reproducer
```kukicha
petiole main

enum Shape
    Circle
        Radius: int
    Square
        Side: int

func mk() Shape
    return Circle{Radius: 3}

func run(s: Shape) string
    return s.nope()
```

- **`8724e1fd^` (and the v0.85.10 tag):** `[semantic/unknown-method] type Shape has no method nope` (exit 1).
- **`8724e1fd` and later (incl. HEAD):** `✓ main.kuki type checks successfully` (exit 0).
- **`kukicha build --skip-build` then `go build`:** `s.nope undefined (type Shape has no field or method nope)` (exit 1).

The same happens for a missing field (`return s.nope`), and for a variant-typed value arriving as a return or field, not only a parameter. Cross-package (qualified `lib.Shape`) still errors, so the regression is exactly the local spelling this commit newly routes to `TypeKindVariant`.

## Root cause
`internal/semantic/semantic_types.go:505-507` now returns `TypeInfo{Kind: TypeKindVariant, …}` for a local variant annotation. But `internal/semantic/semantic_calls_methods.go:1774-1776` (`resolveMethodType`) and `:1500-1502` (`resolveFieldType`) short-circuit with `return nil, false` for non-`Named`/`Struct` kinds, so the caller's gate (`methodResolved && !methodExistsOnType`, `:774-776`) never fires. Before the change the annotation was `TypeKindNamed`, the resolver consulted the symbol table, and a miss was final.

## Fix direction
Teach `resolveMethodType`/`resolveFieldType` (or a small helper) that `TypeKindVariant` is a loaded type: resolve its member tables via the symbol table and return `(nil, true)` for a verified miss. More generally, audit every `(type, resolved)` resolver for the newly-produced kind (see the `compiler-internals` skill's "Changing a type kind or a resolution path" section).

## Verification
Add a red-first test (fails on the parent, passes after): a local `enum Shape` with `func run(s: Shape): return s.nope()` must emit `semantic/unknown-method`. Confirm the parent commit diagnoses it.
record.title: semantic: local variant-typed values lose unknown-method/unknown-field (check-green, go-build-red)

# semantic: alias to a non-`Named` stdlib alias loses `unknown-field` (check-green, `go build`-red)

## Summary
`e8f04fc3` (cross-package type-alias resolution) changed `resolveTypeSymbol` so the `(type, resolved)` flag is set from the **terminal** symbol of an alias chain instead of the start. When the chain ends at a stdlib alias whose kind is not `TypeKindNamed` (a map/list/function alias such as `mcp.JSONObject`), `resolveTypeSymbol` returns the alias with `resolved=false`, so `resolveFieldType`/`resolveMethodType` stay silent and `kukicha check` passes while `go build` fails. Introduced by that commit (the pre-fix compiler diagnosed it).

## Reproducer
```kukicha
petiole main

import "stdlib/mcp"

type Meta = mcp.JSONObject

func Use(m: Meta) any
    return m.Missing
```

- **v0.85.10 (pre-fix):** `[semantic/unknown-field] type Meta has no field Missing` (exit 1).
- **`e8f04fc3` and later (incl. HEAD):** `✓ main.kuki type checks successfully` (exit 0).
- **`go build` on the emitted Go:** `m.Missing undefined` (exit 1).

## Root cause
`internal/semantic/semantic_helpers.go:669-728` (`resolveTypeSymbol`): the stdlib-alias branch requires `gt.Kind == TypeKindNamed` (`:701`). For `mcp.JSONObject` (`generatedStdlibTypeAliases["mcp.JSONObject"] = {Kind: TypeKindMap, …}`) the chain breaks, `underSym` remains the alias, and `resolved` stays false. Consumers at `semantic_calls_methods.go:1515` (`resolveFieldType`) / `:1801` (`resolveMethodType`) then suppress the diagnostic. Later tiers (`GetStdlibStructField`, the live loader) all miss a non-struct alias.

## Fix direction
After the alias loop, when the target is a known stdlib alias whose underlying kind is not `Named`/`Struct`, return a value that lets the resolver set `resolved=true` for a genuinely memberless type (a sentinel "inspected, memberless"), or have `resolveFieldType`/`resolveMethodType` consult `stdlibAliasUnderlying(underlyingName)` (as `aliasUnderlying` does) and mark resolved when the underlying kind is not `Named`/`Struct`.

## Verification
Add a red-first row: `TestCrossPackage_FieldAccessOnStdlibMapAlias` asserting `semantic/unknown-field` on a missing member of a `type X = mcp.JSONObject` value; confirm v0.85.10 is red.
record.title: semantic: alias to a non-Named stdlib alias loses unknown-field (check-green, go-build-red)

# codegen: producer alias dropped when the consumer imports the same dir under another alias -> unbound qualifier (`go build`-red)

## Summary
`7472ee94` (issue #217) resolves a dependency-spelled type qualifier through `AnalysisResult.QualifierImportPaths`, but that provenance map is keyed by the alias the **consumer's** cross-package loader happened to use (`LoadCrossPackageEnvs` is first-write-wins keyed by `q.alias` and dedups by absolute directory). When the consumer also imports the producing directory directly under a different alias, the producer's alias never becomes a key, and codegen emits the producer's spelling with no import bound to it — `kukicha check` passes, `go build` fails with `undefined: <qualifier>`.

## Reproducer (three-package module)
- `internal/types`: exports `type TokenID string`.
- `internal/models`: `import ".../internal/types" as tk` and exports `type MoveAction` with a field `TokenID: tk.TokenID`.
- consumer `main.kuki`: imports `models` **and** `import ".../internal/types" as tokpkg`, then uses `models.MoveAction`.

Observed (HEAD): `kukicha check` is clean, but the emitted Go contains `func() tk.TokenID { … }` with the import block carrying `tokpkg ".../internal/types"` — no `tk` binding — so `go build` fails `undefined: tk`. Removing the consumer's direct `tokpkg` import makes the same producer-alias case work (via `addImportAliased`).

A second, related shape: when the consumer holds a **bare** import of `path` while the producer aliased the package (`pkgPart != extractPkgName(path)`), `qualifyProvenanceRef`'s `alias == ""` arm (`internal/codegen/codegen_types.go:287`) returns `pkgPart + typePart` unbound.

## Root cause
`internal/project/crosspackage.go:104-132` (BFS dedup) + `internal/semantic/semantic_pass.go:342-354` (provenance keyed by alias) + `internal/codegen/codegen_types.go:236-302`. The provenance map cannot represent "the producer spelled this path as `tk`" when the consumer's own alias for that directory won the key.

## Fix direction
Carry producer-side alias provenance across the BFS dedup — key provenance by `(alias, path)` pairs collected from each dependency's own import table, or additionally record `extractPkgName(path)->path` so the codegen local-binding lookup can match by path. In the bare-import arm, route through `addImportAliased(path, pkgPart)` instead of returning an unbound qualifier.

## Verification
Add an end-to-end fixture through `compile()` (`cmd/kukicha/compile_crosspackage_test.go`) with a consumer that imports the producing directory under a second alias, asserting the emitted import block binds the spelling used. The existing `codegen_issue217_test.go` tests inject `QualifierImportPaths` by hand, which the real loader cannot produce for this shape.

## Note
The review classified the underlying BFS mechanism as pre-existing (the failing scenario failed before `7472ee94` too), so this does not block that PR; it is filed because the check-green/build-red seam is live at HEAD.
record.title: codegen: producer alias dropped when the consumer imports the same dir under another alias -> unbound qualifier
